what: speed-sol-items: memoize drop glue per type, as rustc does (`needs_drop_raw`, `is_freeze_raw`). Today `hir_ty::drop::has_drop_glue` and `is_freeze` are plain functions: each of their 18 callers (MIR transform, borrowck, const qualifs, codegen, lints) walks the type field by field again, a `destructor` and `field_types` read and an `instantiate` per field each time, so a body of n locals of a struct of k nested fields costs n*k where the bound is once per distinct type. Exact edit: in `crates/hir-ty/src/db.rs` `kinds!`, after `STRUCT_TAIL_MAY_BE_UNSIZED = 0x2457`, add `DROP_GLUE = 0x2458, "drop_glue_query";` and `IS_FREEZE = 0x2459, "is_freeze_query";`. Then in `crates/hir-ty/src/drop.rs` (speed-sol-items will write it once the kinds exist, or db may): `#[salsa::tracked(returns(copy), mem_tag = Infer)] pub fn drop_glue_query(db: &Db, ty: StoredTy, env: StoredParamEnvAndCrate) -> DropGlue` building one `InferCtxt` in `TypingMode::non_body_analysis()` as `layout_of_ty_query` does, and `has_drop_glue` going through it when `!ty.has_infer() && !ty.has_opaque_types()` (an opaque or inference variable depends on the caller typing mode, so those keep the walk). Same for `is_freeze`. Answers are the same: the walk reads only the type, the env and the typing mode, and the memo is used only where the mode cannot change the answer.
